title: Ledger and Parish
premise: True-crime podcaster Ulyana Galloway reopens the 1997 disappearance of Marisol Vance, a bookkeeper who allegedly embezzled from the parish of St. Brannoc before vanishing. When Ulyana acquires Marisol's diary and finds entries dated years after the disappearance, she realizes Marisol lived in hiding—and that someone in the parish has been hunting her ever since. As Ulyana digs, the town's founding families close ranks, her sources start dying 'accidentally,' and the diary's final entry names a witness the coroner certified dead decades ago. Ulyana finds the witness alive in a coastal care home, exposes the parish's inheritance scheme built on Marisol's stolen identity, and forces a confession before the statute-bound trial begins—though the price is learning that her own grandmother helped build the ledger that started it all.
about_author: V. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former parish archivist turned novelist who spent a decade cataloguing small-town land records before turning to crime fiction. They write from a converted vestry on the Cornish coast, where the tide still dictates the mail schedule.

chapters.title: The Date That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ulyana, narrating in first person, plays a listener voicemail claiming Marisol Vance's diary continued past 1997. She obtains a photocopy of the diary page and confirms the handwriting. The emotional beat is the thrill of the hunt curdling into unease—someone mailed this tip deliberately, and Ulyana doesn't yet ask herself why.

chapters.title: Parish of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ulyana travels to the coastal town of Penmarrick and interviews the aging verger and the Vance family's surviving lawyer, both rehearsed to the point of comedy. Third-person limited follows Ulyana through a town that performs grief like liturgy. The emotional beat is isolation: she's welcomed warmly and warned coldly in the same breath.

chapters.title: Entries in a Borrowed Hand
chapters.summary: A forensic document examiner confirms the diary is authentic—and that the final third was written by someone else imitating Marisol. Ulyana realizes the diary was staged as a false trail. The beat is vertigo: the evidence she staked her reputation on was planted, meaning the planter wanted it found.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: In third person from the perspective of Aldous Crane, the parish treasurer's son, we see him burning documents in the church crypt and making a call to someone about 'the podcaster.' The chapter reveals the parish's founding families still control an inheritance trust built on Marisol's declared death. The beat is menace with manners.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Ulyana's key source, a retired coastguard, dies in a boating 'accident' hours before their meeting. Searching his boat, she finds a photograph of Marisol alive in 2003 and a note: 'Ask the one they buried twice.' The beat is grief and guilt—Ulyana's podcast got him killed.

chapters.title: Dead on Paper
chapters.summary: Ulyana tracks the coroner's 1999 death certificate for the witness, Thomas Renwick, and finds the burial plot empty. A grudging ally, Detective Sergeant Idris Okonkwo, risks his career to unseal the file. The beat is fragile alliance—two lonely people choosing to trust each other against a town.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Crane's POV: he confronts his dying father, who confesses the original embezzlement was invented to cover the family's theft of Marisol's inheritance, and that Renwick saw everything. The beat is inherited rot—power passed down like a curse, each generation deepening the grave.

chapters.title: Salt and Silence
chapters.summary: Following the coastguard's note, Ulyana finds Renwick alive in a care home under a false name, mute from a stroke but lucid. He communicates by pointing at hymn numbers, which map to parish ledger pages. The beat is hushed revelation—witness and seeker finding a language between them.

chapters.title: The Trial of the Tide
chapters.summary: Crane, desperate, tries to burn the care home records with Renwick inside; Ulyana and Okonkwo intervene, and Crane's confession is captured on Ulyana's running recorder. The beat is the climax: fire, exposure, and Crane realizing too late that his father's sin has become his own verdict.

chapters.title: Closing the Book
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Marisol—alive, elderly, and finally willing to testify—meets Ulyana and explains she staged the diary to lure someone brave enough to finish her escape. Ulyana discovers her own grandmother's name in the trust's founding ledger. The beat is bittersweet resolution: justice served, family redefined, and the next case whispering.
